<thought>Using the DBE formula DBE = (2C + 2 + N – H – X)/2 with C=8, H=9, N=1, X=1 gives a non‑integer result, indicating the halogen should be treated as a hydrogen equivalent. Ignoring the halogen in the calculation (as commonly done) yields DBE = C – H/2 + N/2 + 1 = 8 – 9/2 + 1/2 + 1 = 5. Therefore, the compound has 5 double bond equivalents.</thought>
<final_answer>5</final_answer>
